---
title: "JQI_PersonalFinances"
output: html_document
---

```{r Step 1, include=TRUE}

# ============================================================
# JQI_PersonalFinances.Rmd
#
# Purpose:
# Examine whether dimensions of objective employment quality
# are associated with respondents' satisfaction with their
# present financial situation.
#
# Primary outcome:
#   GSS satfin
#
# Primary predictors:
#   compensation
#   benefits
#   earnings_stability
#
# Note:
# JQI measures are assigned at the industry-year level.
# Individual-level standard errors should therefore be treated
# as descriptive until an appropriate assignment-level
# inference strategy is established.
# ============================================================


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Setup
# ------------------------------------------------------------

library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(fixest)
library(car)
library(broom)
library(modelsummary)

options(scipen = 999)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Load GSS + JQI data
# ------------------------------------------------------------

gss_jq <- readRDS(
  here(
    "01_tidydata",
    "GSS_Data_Cleaned",
    "gss_job_quality_primary_2000_2024.rds"
  )
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Construct financial satisfaction measure
# ------------------------------------------------------------
#
# GSS satfin:
#
# 1 = Pretty well satisfied
# 2 = More or less satisfied
# 3 = Not satisfied at all
#
# Reverse-code so that higher values indicate greater
# satisfaction with one's present financial situation:
#
# 3 = Pretty well satisfied
# 2 = More or less satisfied
# 1 = Not satisfied at all
#
# Special missing values are converted to NA.
# ------------------------------------------------------------

gss_jq <- gss_jq %>%
  mutate(
    satfin_num = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(satfin)),

    financial_satisfaction = case_when(
      satfin_num == 1 ~ 3,
      satfin_num == 2 ~ 2,
      satfin_num == 3 ~ 1,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    )
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Inspect the outcome
# ------------------------------------------------------------

gss_jq %>%
  count(financial_satisfaction) %>%
  mutate(
    percent = 100 * n / sum(n)
  )


summary(gss_jq$financial_satisfaction)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Define the primary analytic sample
# ------------------------------------------------------------

jqi_satfin <- gss_jq %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(financial_satisfaction),
    !is.na(compensation),
    !is.na(benefits),
    !is.na(earnings_stability)
  )


# Basic sample description

nrow(jqi_satfin)

jqi_satfin %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean_financial_satisfaction = mean(
      financial_satisfaction,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    sd_financial_satisfaction = sd(
      financial_satisfaction,
      na.rm = TRUE
    )
  )


# Distribution of the outcome in the analytic sample

jqi_satfin %>%
  count(financial_satisfaction) %>%
  mutate(
    percent = 100 * n / sum(n)
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Descriptive statistics for JQI components
# ------------------------------------------------------------

jqi_satfin %>%
  summarise(
    compensation_mean = mean(compensation, na.rm = TRUE),
    compensation_sd = sd(compensation, na.rm = TRUE),

    benefits_mean = mean(benefits, na.rm = TRUE),
    benefits_sd = sd(benefits, na.rm = TRUE),

    earnings_stability_mean = mean(
      earnings_stability,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    earnings_stability_sd = sd(
      earnings_stability,
      na.rm = TRUE
    )
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Bivariate component models
# ------------------------------------------------------------
#
# These reproduce the first stage of the job-satisfaction
# analysis, but with financial satisfaction as the outcome.
# ------------------------------------------------------------

m_fin_compensation <- lm(
  financial_satisfaction ~ compensation,
  data = jqi_satfin
)

m_fin_benefits <- lm(
  financial_satisfaction ~ benefits,
  data = jqi_satfin
)

m_fin_earnings_stability <- lm(
  financial_satisfaction ~ earnings_stability,
  data = jqi_satfin
)


summary(m_fin_compensation)
summary(m_fin_benefits)
summary(m_fin_earnings_stability)


# Compact coefficient table

bind_rows(
  tidy(m_fin_compensation) %>%
    filter(term == "compensation") %>%
    mutate(component = "Compensation"),

  tidy(m_fin_benefits) %>%
    filter(term == "benefits") %>%
    mutate(component = "Benefits"),

  tidy(m_fin_earnings_stability) %>%
    filter(term == "earnings_stability") %>%
    mutate(component = "Earnings stability")
) %>%
  select(
    component,
    estimate,
    std.error,
    statistic,
    p.value
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 8. Correlations among JQI components
# ------------------------------------------------------------

jqi_satfin %>%
  select(
    compensation,
    benefits,
    earnings_stability
  ) %>%
  cor(use = "complete.obs")


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 9. Joint component model
# ------------------------------------------------------------

m_fin_components <- lm(
  financial_satisfaction ~
    compensation +
    benefits +
    earnings_stability,
  data = jqi_satfin
)

summary(m_fin_components)

jqi_satfin %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    years = n_distinct(year),
    industries = n_distinct(industry_common),
    industry_year_cells = n_distinct(
      paste(year, industry_common)
    )
  )
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 10. Multicollinearity
# ------------------------------------------------------------

vif(m_fin_components)



yearly_fin_models <- jqi_satfin %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  nest() %>%
  mutate(
    model = map(
      data,
      ~ lm(
        financial_satisfaction ~
          compensation +
          benefits +
          earnings_stability,
        data = .x
      )
    ),
    results = map(
      model,
      ~ tidy(.x)
    )
  ) %>%
  unnest(results) %>%
  filter(
    term %in% c(
      "compensation",
      "benefits",
      "earnings_stability"
    )
  )


yearly_fin_models %>%
  select(
    year,
    term,
    estimate,
    std.error,
    statistic,
    p.value
  ) %>%
  print(n = Inf)


yearly_fin_models %>%
  distinct(year) %>%
  left_join(
    jqi_satfin %>%
      count(year, name = "n"),
    by = "year"
  )

m_fin_component_year <- lm(
  financial_satisfaction ~
    compensation * factor(year) +
    benefits * factor(year) +
    earnings_stability * factor(year),
  data = jqi_satfin
)

summary(m_fin_component_year)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Formal tests of temporal heterogeneity
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# Compensation × year
compensation_year_terms <- grep(
  "compensation:factor\\(year\\)|factor\\(year\\).*:compensation",
  names(coef(m_fin_component_year)),
  value = TRUE
)

linearHypothesis(
  m_fin_component_year,
  compensation_year_terms
)


# Benefits × year
benefits_year_terms <- grep(
  "benefits:factor\\(year\\)|factor\\(year\\).*:benefits",
  names(coef(m_fin_component_year)),
  value = TRUE
)

linearHypothesis(
  m_fin_component_year,
  benefits_year_terms
)


# Earnings stability × year
earnings_stability_year_terms <- grep(
  "earnings_stability:factor\\(year\\)|factor\\(year\\).*:earnings_stability",
  names(coef(m_fin_component_year)),
  value = TRUE
)

linearHypothesis(
  m_fin_component_year,
  earnings_stability_year_terms
)

#Benefits has the clearest positive independent association with financial satisfaction, compensation has a much smaller conditional association, and earnings stability has a distinct negative association.
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 11. Save primary model objects
# ------------------------------------------------------------

saveRDS(
  m_fin_compensation,
  here(
    "01_tidydata",
    "GSS_Data_Cleaned",
    "model_financial_satisfaction_compensation.rds"
  )
)

saveRDS(
  m_fin_benefits,
  here(
    "01_tidydata",
    "GSS_Data_Cleaned",
    "model_financial_satisfaction_benefits.rds"
  )
)

saveRDS(
  m_fin_earnings_stability,
  here(
    "01_tidydata",
    "GSS_Data_Cleaned",
    "model_financial_satisfaction_earnings_stability.rds"
  )
)

saveRDS(
  m_fin_components,
  here(
    "01_tidydata",
    "GSS_Data_Cleaned",
    "model_financial_satisfaction_components.rds"
  )
)
```
